scope.evidence_basis: Actual isolated canonical readings, current mechanism/body reread, and cached original-source verification. Local examples and the scalar comparison calculation were recomputed; no independent review is claimed.

N-M-riccati: Construct the radial Jacobi tensor, prove symmetry of S, and derive the Riccati equation.
State the singular matrix comparison input and identify S with the distance Hessian before cut time.
Integrate the Jacobi logarithmic derivative and exclude an earlier conjugate point in the upper-sectional branch.
N-M-trace: Take the Riccati trace and apply Cauchy–Schwarz under the Ricci lower bound.
Prove the singular scalar comparison with an integrating factor.
Identify the Laplacian and determinant derivative, and explain the loss of directional information.
N-M-cut-integration: Truncate polar density at cut time and use the measure-zero cut-locus integration theorem.
Differentiate the weighted average and justify monotonicity and the small-radius limit.
Use Bonnet–Myers and saturated model volume to extend the positive-curvature result to all radii.
N-M-myers: Sum the sine-test index forms and evaluate the negative integral when L exceeds D_k.
Use Hopf–Rinow and the complete universal Riemannian cover to obtain compactness and finite fundamental group.
N-M-hadamard: Use convexity of the squared Jacobi norm to exclude conjugate points.
Prove completeness of the exponential pullback metric by the one-base-point Hopf–Rinow criterion.
Apply the complete-local-isometry covering interface and explain the role of simple connectivity.
N-M-toponogov: Connect local Rauch comparison to local angle comparison and state the precise shrinking-hinge input.
Estimate distances between successive violating hinges and use completeness to reach a local contradiction.
Distinguish the SSS angle, same-angle hinge and SSS chord conclusions and identify the imported conversion.

N-R-rauch.objects: Normal Jacobi field on a given unit geodesic in a smooth n-manifold.
N-R-rauch.domain: Times 0<t<min(T,D_k); only the lower-sectional direction assumes no actual conjugate point through T.
N-R-rauch.fixed_and_variable: Fixed n,k,geodesic and derivative norm a; field/time vary.
N-R-rauch.hypotheses: Radial plane bounds are quantified along the segment; no global completeness is needed.
N-R-rauch.equations: J(0)=0, |D_tJ(0)|=a>0 and s solves the unit-normalized model ODE.
N-R-rauch.quantifiers: Every radial plane and every stated time are covered, with separate hypothesis branches.
N-R-rauch.conclusion: Upper sectional bound gives length >= model; lower gives <= before actual conjugacy.
N-R-rauch.status: Known comparison, conservatively specialized from matrix comparison; no original result claim.
N-R-rauch.local_definitions: Normal Jacobi field is defined in N-D-jacobi; s and D_k are defined inside this statement.

N-R-hessian.objects: Distance from a fixed point on a complete smooth n-manifold.
N-R-hessian.domain: Regular distance domain and 0<ell<D_k are explicitly imposed.
N-R-hessian.fixed_and_variable: The metric, p,x,k and its unique radial segment are fixed; all tangent X are tested.
N-R-hessian.hypotheses: Only sectional bounds on planes tangent to that segment are needed.
N-R-hessian.equations: The RHS retains |X|²−dr(X)² and s prime/s with normalized ODE.
N-R-hessian.quantifiers: Every tangent vector, both curvature directions; no tensor estimate asserted at a cut point.
N-R-hessian.conclusion: Lower curvature yields Hessian <= model, upper curvature reverses it.
N-R-hessian.status: Established local specialization of the matrix theorem; reverse direction identified as a deduction.
N-R-hessian.local_definitions: r,ell,s,D_k are supplied locally; Cut(p) is the named standard geometric input.

N-R-laplacian.objects: Distance function on a connected complete smooth n-manifold.
N-R-laplacian.fixed_and_variable: Fix metric,k, then each p and regular x.
N-R-laplacian.hypotheses: Ric >= (n−1)k g is global, without an unstated sectional requirement.
N-R-laplacian.equations: Delta=div grad; coefficient (n−1)s prime/s matches the trace convention.
N-R-laplacian.quantifiers: For every base point and every regular point in range.
N-R-laplacian.conclusion: A scalar upper bound only; no reversed or directional bound implied.
N-R-laplacian.status: Known theorem supported by actual trace-comparison sections.
N-R-laplacian.local_definitions: Model s,D_k and r are defined within the canonical block.

N-R-bishop-gromov.objects: Volumes of metric balls in complete smooth n-manifolds and the same-dimensional simply connected model.
N-R-bishop-gromov.domain: All positive radii; spherical model volume is explicitly saturated.
N-R-bishop-gromov.fixed_and_variable: Fixed metric and k, arbitrary p and ordered r<R.
N-R-bishop-gromov.hypotheses: The normalized Ricci lower bound and completeness are retained.
N-R-bishop-gromov.equations: Both ratio inequality and small-radius limit appear; no density sine continued past D_k.
N-R-bishop-gromov.quantifiers: Every center and every pair 0<r<R; no absolute lower volume bound.
N-R-bishop-gromov.conclusion: Nonincreasing ratio bounded above by one; equivalent growth inequality.
N-R-bishop-gromov.status: Known result; equality assertions are separate nodes.
N-R-bishop-gromov.local_definitions: Model V_k^n and its positive-curvature extension are locally identified.

N-R-myers.objects: Connected complete smooth Riemannian n-manifold without boundary.
N-R-myers.fixed_and_variable: One common k>0 for the whole manifold.
N-R-myers.hypotheses: The Ricci inequality is quantified for every x and tangent v.
N-R-myers.quantifiers: Uniform positive k precedes universal point/vector quantifiers.
N-R-myers.conclusion: Compactness, diameter bound and finite fundamental group.
N-R-myers.status: Classical theorem; exact sine-index mechanism checked, original1941 unread.
N-R-myers.local_definitions: Ricci convention in N-D-curvature; no hidden model notation in the block.

N-R-hadamard.objects: Exponential map at each point of a complete smooth nonpositively curved manifold.
N-R-hadamard.domain: Global tangent space maps onto M; no boundary intended under project convention.
N-R-hadamard.fixed_and_variable: The metric is fixed and p is arbitrary.
N-R-hadamard.hypotheses: Sectional nonpositivity and completeness; simple connectivity only for the stronger branch.
N-R-hadamard.quantifiers: For every p; the conditional simply connected conclusion is separate.
N-R-hadamard.conclusion: Covering always; diffeomorphism and unique minimizing connections with simple connectivity.
N-R-hadamard.status: Known theorem with the covering/path-lifting input explicitly imported.
N-R-hadamard.local_definitions: Standard exp and simple connectivity are reader inputs, not conflated with Ricci or absence of cut points.

N-R-toponogov.objects: Chosen minimizing triangle in a complete smooth Riemannian n-manifold and a constant-curvature model surface.
N-R-toponogov.domain: Strict triangle inequalities and perimeter <2D_k; no antipodal endpoint assertion.
N-R-toponogov.fixed_and_variable: Fix k and actual side representatives; compare separately SSS and SAS data.
N-R-toponogov.hypotheses: Global sectional lower bound, completeness, n>=2 and admissible model size.
N-R-toponogov.equations: Angles >=, SAS opposite side <=, SSS matched cross-distance >=.
N-R-toponogov.quantifiers: Each angle and all matched side points are included; sides in M need not be unique.
N-R-toponogov.conclusion: Three compatible comparisons under distinct fixed-data experiments.
N-R-toponogov.status: Known theorem, checked against original angle statement and modern full formulation.
N-R-toponogov.local_definitions: D_k, model surface, side matching and hinge matching are specified locally.

findings: Recovered the focused question with exactly seven interfaces, strict triangle perimeter and smooth-distance domains; broad equality and endpoint gaps remain unaltered.

Reread all seven canonical principals alone. Rauch keeps the actual conjugate hypothesis only in the lower-sectional branch, Hessian retains the zero radial direction, Laplacian uses unnormalized Ricci, and Bishop–Gromov uses saturated spherical volume for all radii.

Reread the foundations bridge: metric completeness, LC connection, normal geodesic variation and Hessian have precise definitions; Gauss, second variation, polar integration and Hopf–Rinow are imported with actual locators.
For Riccati, checked the vanishing Wronskian, symmetric operator, U=GZG^T comparison and shared t^{-1} pole interface; integrated log|J| and retained the first-conjugate bootstrap.

For trace comparison, w=a-c_k satisfies w′+(a+c_k)w<=0; the integrating factor behaves as Ct^2 and kills the O(t) initial difference. Determinant differentiation and trace identify exactly the scalar outputs.

For polar integration, zero after the cut produces downward jumps; q is nonincreasing and the weighted-average derivative is nonpositive almost everywhere. Local absolute continuity and the small-radius limit complete the comparison. Myers supplies the positive-k large radii.
Summed the sine-test index forms and checked (n-1)L((pi/L)^2-k)/2. Geodesic lifting makes the universal-cover metric complete, and a closed discrete fiber inside a compact cover is finite.

For Hadamard, convex squared Jacobi norm precludes return to zero; every geodesic from zero in the pullback metric is radial and extends, justifying the one-base-point Hopf–Rinow use. Covering does not by itself imply injectivity.

For Toponogov, checked Lang pp.63–70 and the exact px union {y} endpoint condition. The 4/5 perimeter contraction yields the 9/5 distance estimate, and all endpoints converge to the same limit; local comparison holds uniformly in a sufficiently small neighborhood. Gluing and the angle/hinge/chord conversion remain imported.

Recomputed model s_k, flat-cylinder cut point without conjugacy, S2xS2 Ric=g with zero mixed curvature, collapse estimate, incomplete ball/hemisphere and torus opposite side 0.2 versus 0.8. The Rauch counterexample now explicitly holds for some t<D_1 after the first actual conjugate time.

The consumed Günther node is only a contextual dependency of the collapse example: its lower bound is restricted to r<min(inj_p,D_k) and follows by integrating the uncut Hessian-derived density. It is not an eighth principal or a promised full proof.
